query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Modify a GitHub-hosted backend application, add protected console and lead-care functionality, configure deployment/runtime infrastructure, apply database migrations, and verify CI plus hosted deployment status.
query_ground_truth.query: verify CI and hosted deployment status
query_ground_truth.intent: Check the status of continuous integration pipelines and confirm the successful deployment of the application on the hosting environment.

requirement_groups.purpose: verify CI status and workflow runs

request.query: verify CI and hosted deployment status

results.use_case: verify CI and hosted deployment status
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Validate the target revision exists using GITHUB_GET_A_COMMIT (avoid checking the wrong artifact and capture basic metadata).
[Optional (if commit identifier is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Resolve the latest revision on the target branch using GITHUB_GET_A_BRANCH (use the resolved SHA for downstream lookups).
[Required] [Step]: Retrieve status contexts using GITHUB_GET_COMMIT_STATUSES (select the newest entry per context; treat older duplicates as stale).
[Optional (if statuses are pending/ambiguous)] [Step]: Cross-check CI conclusions using GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF (confirm the latest run matches the newest status context).

[Fallback (if no reliable deployment match can be derived from statuses)] [Step]: Locate the matching deployment using VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENTS (filter by commit/ref when possible, handle data.pagination, pick newest relevant by time/readyState).
[Required] [Step]: Confirm deployment outcome using VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENT (record readyState/state and any promotion/alias indicators; focus on key fields if payload is huge).
[Required] [Step]: Determine pass/fail/gated conditions using VERCEL_LIST_DEPLOYMENT_CHECKS (identify specific blocking signals when not successful).
[Optional (if deployment is not in a final state)] [Next Step]: Poll by re-calling VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENT until a terminal readyState is reached, then re-evaluate outcome fields.
[Optional (if deeper root-cause is needed)] [Next Step]: Retrieve stage-level failure context using VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENT_EVENTS2 (pinpoint failing phase).
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_GET_COMMIT_STATUSES] Status entries may be empty even when check runs exist; don’t treat absence as success.
[GITHUB_GET_COMMIT_STATUSES] The same context can appear multiple times; selecting a non-newest item can report outdated pending/success.
[VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENTS] Results live under data.deployments with a separate data.pagination object; don’t assume a flat list or array order.
[VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENT] Responses can be very large and may be truncated by clients; extract specific fields (readyState/state/related indicators).
[VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENT] Wrong or inaccessible identifiers can return HTTP 404 (not_found); prefer IDs obtained from VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENTS.

GITHUB_GET_COMMIT_STATUSES.description: List all statuses for a commit reference (SHA, branch, or tag) in reverse chronological order. Use when you need to check CI/CD status results from various systems for a specific commit.

ref.description: The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (heads/BRANCH_NAME), or tag name (tags/TAG_NAME).

page.description: Page number of results to fetch. Default: 1

repo.description: The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

per_page.description: Number of results per page, maximum 100. Default: 30

VERCEL_GET_DEPLOYMENTS.description: Tool to list deployments from Vercel. Use when you need to retrieve deployment information for a project or team.

to.description: Gets the deployment created before this Date timestamp. (default: current time)

from.description: Gets the deployment created after this Date timestamp. (default: current time)

branch.description: The name of the branch. Cannot contain wildcard characters. To use wildcard characters in branch names, use [the GraphQL API](https://docs.github.com/graphql). If 'HEAD' is provided, it will be resolved to the repository's default branch.
